# Load forecast and uncertainty: one-page analysis

*Generated by scripts/06_write_reports.py from the latest run.*

**Model and features.** The load is a production schedule: plant state × day type × quarter-hour explains ~97 % of
its variance (script 02). Feature groups were tested on two December-like holdout months (November trained on
Jan–Oct, January trained on Feb–Nov) and the simplest group within 1 % of the best was kept: **core**
(qh, dow, is_weekend, is_holiday, state_SHUTDOWN, state_MAINTENANCE, state_RAMP_UP, state_NORMAL, state_HIGH_DEMAND).

| Feature group | Holdout MAE NORMAL (kW) | CV MAE NORMAL (kW) |
|---|---|---|
| core | 9.69 | 9.57 |
| core + cyclic | 9.70 | 9.58 |
| core + temperature | 9.75 | 9.64 |
| core + season | 18.18 | 9.90 |

Month and week of year were excluded: they re-encode the plant state, never take December values in training, and
29–31 Dec wrap to ISO week 1 (CV cannot reveal this; the November holdout does). Temperature and sin/cos added no
measurable gain. Selected model: **xgboost**, chosen by expected December error
(0.935 × holdout NORMAL MAE + 0.065 × CV SHUTDOWN MAE):

| Model | NORMAL MAE Nov / Jan (kW) | CV SHUTDOWN MAE (kW) | December score |
|---|---|---|---|
| xgboost | 9.59 / 9.79 | 1.69 | 9.17 |
| lightgbm | 9.60 / 9.77 | 2.05 | 9.19 |
| random_forest | 9.92 / 10.05 | 1.61 | 9.44 |
| xgboost_shallow | 9.96 / 10.03 | 17.72 | 10.50 |
| profile | 11.68 / 11.78 | 2.00 | 11.10 |
| ridge | 39.03 / 36.69 | 38.70 | 37.91 |

**Metrics.** MAE is primary (kW; cost is linear in load), RMSE punishes large misses, WAPE compares states, bias shows
drift. MAPE is rejected (shutdown load is as low as 28 kW).

| Plant state | CV MAE (kW) | WAPE | Interval coverage P10–P90 | Mean width (kW) | December avg ± (P10–P90) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NORMAL | 9.6 | 3.6 % | 79.8 % | 30.6 | 265.2 ± 15.3 kW |
| SHUTDOWN | 1.7 | 3.5 % | 82.0 % | 5.7 | 34.6 ± 16.1 kW |
| HIGH_DEMAND | 17.3 | 5.9 % | 79.6 % | 52.1 | not present in test period |
| MAINTENANCE | 5.2 | 6.6 % | 80.7 % | 16.8 | not present in test period |
| RAMP_UP | 35.4 | 32.5 % | 53.7 % | 52.2 | not present in test period |

**Does performance vary by condition?** Yes: absolute errors are largest in busy, volatile states, relative errors at
low load; errors peak at the shift changes (06:00, 14:00, 22:00); forward-chaining fails on states never seen before
(April 29.4 kW, July 111.4 kW, August 74.6 kW vs
~10 kW otherwise). Two workdays whose load contradicts their label (1 Aug RAMP_UP running at full load, 15 Aug
HIGH_DEMAND at ramp-up load) were excluded from training.

**Uncertainty.** Intervals = point forecast + out-of-sample residual quantiles per plant state × day type × shift.
Cross-fitted coverage: 78.8 % for P10–P90 (target 80 %), 88.4 % for P5–P95
(target 90 %); holdout NORMAL rows 78.4 % (Nov) and
79.6 % (Jan). P10/P90 is delivered because Strategy B uses P90 and 10 %
tails calibrate reliably per condition. **Intervals widen for harder states:** widest in RAMP_UP and HIGH_DEMAND, on
workdays and in the day shifts; narrowest in SHUTDOWN and at night. One global width would over-cover low-load states
and under-cover HIGH_DEMAND.

**Why plant_state matters.** It sets the load level (≈ 28–360 kW) and the error size, and it is known in advance.
SHUTDOWN on a holiday (25–26 Dec) never occurred: tree models would predict ≈ 0 kW, so a data-driven rule places it
between the shutdown weekend and workday levels (holiday weight w = 0.216), with an envelope interval
(25 Dec: P10 28.0, P50 34.9, P90 61.5 kW).

**Data quality and forecast availability.** Non-GOOD rows (weather missing, wrong or unverifiable), isolated spikes and
the two mislabelled days were excluded; the load was never imputed. The model uses temperature: False;
the simulated widening factor for the 64 December rows without a weather forecast is 1.000.
